panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 6 panels (A, B, C, D, E, F). A: The panel shows T1 hyperintensity in the globus pallidus, which is explicitly linked in the caption to CO poisoning. B: Shows hemorrhagic infarction in the posterior parietal regions, which is a characteristic presentation of carbon monoxide poisoning as described in the text. C: Shows T2 hyperintensity in the subcortical white matter consistent with diffuse hypoxic injury characteristic of CO poisoning. D: Shows T2 hyperintensity in the globus pallidus, correlating with known CO poisoning findings in this context. E: The FLAIR image demonstrates abnormal white matter signals (hyperintensities) which are described as representing diffuse hypoxic white matter injury. F: SWI demonstrates signal dropout in the globus pallidus and posterior occipital region, indicative of microhemorrhage or iron deposition secondary to hypoxia/CO poisoning.

in_text_mentions: tic resonance venography of the brain were performed which showed abnormal signal intensity areas and almost symmetric involvement of bilateral cerebral hemispheres involving the posterior parietal and occipital lobes, which appeared hyperintense on T1/T2-weighted images with a peripheral rim of hypointensity. Corresponding areas showed signal dropouts on susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI) sequence. No postcontrast meningeal or parenchymal enhancement was noted. No cerebral venous sinus thrombosis was found. Findings were representative of hemorrhagic infarctions (Figure 1, Panels B, C, F).

Bilateral symmetrical signals were seen in the corona radiata and periventricular regions, representing diffuse hypoxic white matter injury (Figure 1, Panels C, E). There were bilateral symmetrical abnormal signals in the globus pallidus on T1/T2-weighted images with signal dropouts on SWI, typical of CO poisoning (Figure 1, Panels A, D, F). There was no hydrocephalus or midline shift. Additionally, the corpus callosum, brainstem, and cerebellum were normal.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 6 panels (A, B, C, D, E, F). A: Panel A shows DWI sequence of the brain showing restricted diffusion in the bilateral globus pallidus, a hallmark of acute cerebral hypoxia in CO poisoning. B: Panel B shows ADC map confirming the restricted diffusion (low signal) in the bilateral globus pallidus. C: Panel C shows T1-weighted image with characteristic hypointensity in the globus pallidus. D: Panel D shows T2-weighted image with characteristic hyperintensity in the globus pallidus. E: Panel E shows FLAIR sequence demonstrating hyperintensity in the bilateral globus pallidus. F: Panel F, gradient echo (GRE), shows tiny foci of increased susceptibility, consistent with associated microvascular injury/microhemorrhages in the context of severe CO poisoning.
